rv.q: The spectacular result is every bit a match for the movie.
Xia's ability to paint vivid stage pictures makes this revival a hit.
Matthew Xia’s production fizzes with so much energy and sly humour that you’re willing to forgive the one-dimensional characterisation.
Had greater liberties been taken with Henzell and Rhone’s screenplay, it could have been so much better.
The singing, individually and, thrillingly, in harmony, is as impressive as I have seen in years – and what songs!
They Come at Stratford East is an absolute treat: a vibrant, moving, and ultimately triumphant piece of musical theatre that reminds us why some songs, and some stories, are truly timeless.
But the story still flounders between high jinx and moral turpitude.
They Come at Stratford East is a vivid, energetic production that honours the cult classic film while breathing new life into it.
Parks’ version, first seen in New York’s Public Theater in 2023, may not receive similar accolades.

cn.t: Critics praise this vibrant adaptation for its energetic staging and iconic reggae soundtrack, with Matthew Xia's direction and Natey Jones's star-making performance bringing the cult 1972 film to vivid life on stage.
